features.statement: Pairs a serif display face for headings and large lede text with a clean sans-serif for UI and body text.
Hero H1 is oversized white bold serif, wrapping onto multiple short lines over a full-bleed photo.
Body text is set slightly large (about 17px) with generous line height around 1.7.
Uses a single magenta-pink accent for buttons, with a deeper berry shade for links and eyebrow labels.
Footer uses muted light pink-grey text with lighter pink links on a dark background.
Section headings are introduced by small uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow labels, including in the hero.
Sections alternate background color fields (cream, dark aubergine, blush, photo strip, dark footer), producing distinct horizontal bands.
Primary call-to-action buttons are fully rounded pills, implemented as styled anchors rather than button elements.
Cards use small-to-medium corner radii while most elements remain square-cornered.
Testimonials are three equal-height white cards with star ratings, quote, and serif name pinned at the bottom, no photos.
Testimonials are marked up semantically with figure, blockquote and figcaption elements.
Blog posts appear as a ruled list with hairline dividers, serif titles left and small author links right.
Social feed appears as a grid of image-less gradient tiles with truncated serif captions.
Standalone emphasized text links are underlined, bold and end with a right-arrow glyph.
Teaser copy is truncated with a trailing ellipsis before a read-more button.
Copy is warm and personal, using sentence fragments and avoiding exclamation marks and em dashes.
Content sits in a centered column about 1080px wide, with only hero, split panel and photo band full-bleed.
Header has a serif wordmark on the left and a row of plain text nav links on the right.
Hero text is left-aligned over a photograph, stacking eyebrow, large heading and a one-line tagline.
Dark botanical photography blends into adjoining dark panels, with a decorative full-width photo band above the footer.
Footer contact details use an address element with linked phone numbers.
Page is built with no scripts and a small set of hand-named, non-utility CSS classes.
